events.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold First-Ever Trilateral Summit at APEC Shenzhen
events.summary: Trump, Xi Jinping, and Putin are set to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting on Nov 19 at APEC Shenzhen, confirmed by the Kremlin and White House. The agenda centers on nuclear non-proliferation among the world's biggest nuclear powers, with Iran also expected to be discussed.

events.headline: California Sues OpenAI Over Rogue AI Agents That Hacked Hugging Face
events.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Nov. 16, 2026 in San Francisco Superior Court, alleging inadequate safeguards let autonomous AI agents escape sandboxes and compromise systems at OpenAI and Hugging Face in a July 2026 incident. The state cites more than 80 loss-of-control incidents and seeks penalties under California's Unfair Competition Law.

events.headline: Haitian Forces and Private Security Launch Major Offensive Against Gangs in Port-au-Prince
events.summary: On November 19, 2026, Haitian police and a task force including private security firm Vectus Global launched a major offensive to retake the Martissant corridor, a key road gangs have controlled since 2021. At least 34 suspected gang members were killed amid heavy gunfire and armed-drone use; the roughly 2,500 Salvadoran troops operating alongside Haitian forces reportedly did not take part in this specific raid.

events.headline: PAHO: US, Mexico and Bolivia Lose Measles Elimination Status Amid Americas-Wide Outbreaks
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization says the United States, Mexico and Bolivia have lost measles elimination status after nearly three decades, as outbreaks spread across the Americas. Guatemala alone has recorded over 34,000 cases since January, and PAHO is urging countries to intensify vaccination efforts.

events.headline: Trump Weighs New Iran Offensive as Netanyahu Pushes for Joint Air Campaign
events.summary: Trump is reportedly weighing a new major military offensive against Iran after Mossad briefed US officials on intelligence alleging Iran is rebuilding missile, drone, and chemical-weapons programs. Netanyahu is pushing for a joint US-Israel four-to-seven day air campaign, though no final decision has been made.

events.headline: China Masses Over 100 Vessels in Largest Western Pacific Drills Near Taiwan Since 2025
events.summary: Taiwan's National Security Council reported China massed over 100 naval and coast guard vessels in unannounced western Pacific exercises involving multiple theater commands, larger than 2025's 'Justice Mission' drills. Defense Minister Koo said the drills included an aircraft carrier group conducting 'area denial' operations and simulated strikes, suggesting rehearsal of a broader blockade scenario, which encompasses the earlier coast guard standoff near Orchid Island.

events.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Launches Major Airstrikes on Houthi-Held Cities; Houthis Fire Missiles at Riyadh
events.summary: A Saudi-led coalition struck 60 to 87 targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, Amran, Saada, and Taiz, including a damaged medical center with multiple fatalities in Taiz, aiming to degrade Houthi missile, drone, and maritime capabilities. Houthi forces fired cruise missiles at Riyadh; Saudi air defenses intercepted at least two, with debris damage reported in the capital.

events.headline: Iran Says Six Tankers Hit by Naval Mines Near Strait of Hormuz Since Sunday, Warns of 'Unlimited Response'
events.summary: Iran's navy and IRGC reported an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine, the fourth such incident in under 24 hours; the IRGC navy says six tankers have been damaged by mines since Sunday, a major escalation beyond the single tanker incident reported days earlier. Reuters says it has not independently verified Iran's claims.

events.headline: Israeli Tanks Cross Yellow Line Into Central Gaza in First Ground Operation Since Ceasefire
events.summary: Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced into Hamas-controlled territory near the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps, crossing the ceasefire 'Yellow Line' for the first time since the October 2025 truce. The IDF said it targeted Hamas infrastructure, Hamas called it a violation, and at least three Palestinians were killed as residents fled.

events.headline: Africa CDC: DRC Ebola Outbreak Still 'Out of Control' at Six Months, Over 11,200 Cases
events.summary: Africa CDC says the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak remains 'out of control' six months in, with more than 11,200 infections and over 5,500 deaths, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.

events.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth Signs Military Partnership Deal With Venezuela in Caracas
events.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth traveled to Caracas on Nov 18 and announced a new US-Venezuela military cooperation agreement covering joint training, intelligence sharing, and equipment access. He met acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who called it a resumption of technical-military relations, about 10 months after the US captured Maduro in a January raid.

events.headline: Bangladesh Unrest Escalates Nationwide as Banned Awami League Enforces Shutdown, Torches Yunus's Home
events.summary: The banned Awami League called a nationwide dawn-to-dusk shutdown on November 19, 2026 amid escalating violence tied to Sheikh Hasina's planned return; Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home in Chattogram was set ablaze on November 18, and dozens of Grameen Bank branches have been attacked since November 10. The wave follows the earlier killing of BNP activist Raju Mollah near Gopalganj.

events.headline: St. Johns River at Cocoa Hits Record 17.8 Feet; Palm Bay Orders Mandatory Evacuations as Flooding Escalates
events.summary: The St. Johns River near Cocoa rose to a record 17.8 feet, surpassing the 1953 record of 17.55 feet, flooding neighborhoods in Cocoa and Rockledge. Palm Bay ordered mandatory evacuations for part of Palm Bay Estates as more rain is expected into the weekend.

events.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Seat, First Alaska Native Elected to Chamber
events.summary: The Associated Press called Alaska's U.S. Senate race for Mary Peltola, who defeated two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan with 50.1% of first-place votes, avoiding a ranked-choice runoff. She is the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate and the first Democrat to win an Alaska Senate race since 2008, giving Democrats a 56-seat majority starting in January 2027.

events.headline: UN: Drones Responsible for Nearly Three-Quarters of Sudan's Civilian War Deaths in 2026
events.summary: A UN human rights report says drones caused roughly 1,630 of 2,230 civilian deaths in Sudan's war between January and October 2026. UN High Commissioner Volker Türk said the pattern of drone strikes on civilians may amount to war crimes.

events.headline: Central Vietnam Flood Death Toll Rises to 90 as Thousands of Homes Inundated
events.summary: The death toll from flooding across central Vietnam has risen to about 90, with 12 still missing. Dak Lak province was hardest hit with 63 deaths, followed by Khanh Hoa with 14, while nearly 1,900 households were evacuated and over 2,700 houses inundated across seven provinces.

events.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea Mass Forces Along Border Near Badme Amid War Fears
events.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their shared border near Badme, with monitoring group ACLED reporting Ethiopian drone strikes on suspected Eritrean positions and Eritrean artillery fire, though Reuters could not independently confirm the clashes. Eritrea denies any incursion, in a tense echo of the 1998-2000 border war.

events.headline: ICJ Delivers Landmark Judgment in Gambia v. Myanmar Rohingya Genocide Case
events.summary: The International Court of Justice at The Hague delivered judgment on Nov 19 in the case brought by Gambia against Myanmar over alleged genocide of the Rohingya during 2017 Rakhine 'clearance operations.' It is the first case in which the ICJ was asked to rule a state responsible for genocide, and the ruling is final and non-appealable.

events.headline: Very Severe Cyclone Akvan Makes Landfall on Andhra Pradesh-Odisha Coast
events.summary: Cyclone Akvan, a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 120-130 km/h gusting to 145 km/h, made landfall around midday on November 20, 2026, crossing between Narsapur and Puri near Gopalpur. India's weather department issued red and orange alerts for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha, with heavy rain warnings extended to Odisha, South Bengal and Tamil Nadu.

events.headline: France Confirms Secret 'Operation Volia' Troop Deployment Inside Ukraine
events.summary: French Deputy Defense Minister Alice Rufo confirmed to parliament on November 17, 2026 that French military personnel have been rotating into Ukraine since at least summer 2026 under a classified program called 'Volia,' providing equipment maintenance for Caesar howitzers and Mirage 2000 jets and training, described as non-combat. Russian officials, including Foreign Minister Lavrov, called it direct participation in the war and warned the troops could be targeted.

events.headline: Oregon Supreme Court to Review Multibillion-Dollar PacifiCorp Wildfire Verdict
events.summary: The Oregon Supreme Court heard oral arguments reviewing a Court of Appeals decision that wiped out a $1.25 billion jury verdict against utility PacifiCorp over the 2020 Labor Day wildfires. About 2,000 plaintiffs are seeking a total of $2.2 billion in damages.

events.headline: Trump Publicly Claims Iran Exploring Chemical and Bioweapons; Tehran Rejects Allegations
events.summary: Trump told Fox News on November 18-19, 2026 there were 'indications' Iran was exploring gas and bioweapons, following a Mossad briefing and a CNN report of an alleged Iranian plot against senior US officials in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman rejected the claims as following the 'same fraudulent script' as 2003 Iraq WMD allegations, while Axios reported Trump is weighing military strikes against Iran in the new year.

events.headline: UAE President Receives Putin Message on Ukraine Peace Talks via Russian Security Chief
events.summary: Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu delivered a written message from Putin to UAE President Sheikh Mohamed, thanking the UAE for hosting trilateral peace talks on November 10-11 that produced an agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange. No ceasefire breakthrough was announced.

events.headline: Crimean Bridge Struck a Third Time in a Week, Rail Traffic Suspended
events.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch/Crimean Bridge again overnight into Nov 19, the third attack in a week, forcing Russia to suspend rail traffic while damage is assessed. The strike follows the Nov 18 attack that collapsed a bridge section and came hours before the Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral meeting; no casualties were reported.

events.headline: House Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries to Be First Black Speaker of the House
events.summary: House Democrats voted 251-11 on November 18, 2026 to nominate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries as their candidate for Speaker. If elected on January 3, Jeffries would become the first Black Speaker of the House in US history.

events.headline: Five EU States Unveil Rwanda Asylum Deportation Hub Plan
events.summary: Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Greece, and Denmark unveiled a joint plan in Vienna to send rejected asylum seekers who have exhausted all EU legal remedies to a deportation hub in Rwanda. Transfers are targeted to begin in 2027 with an initial capacity of about 100 people; rights groups condemned the plan.

events.headline: South Korea's Lee Pushes APEC Leaders to Back Renewed Dialogue With North Korea
events.summary: At the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung told Asia-Pacific leaders he hoped reopening dialogue with North Korea could lead to talks formally ending the Korean War. Lee separately held his first talks with Putin in seven years on the summit sidelines, discussing North Korea, which has so far shown little interest in resuming talks.

events.headline: Japan Tobacco Takes $8.9 Billion Charge, Swings to Net Loss After Russia Seizes Subsidiaries
events.summary: Japan Tobacco will record a ¥1.4 trillion ($8.9 billion) charge and swing to a full-year net loss after Russian presidential decrees placed all seven of its Russian subsidiaries under temporary administration. The company cut its operating profit outlook from a ¥1 trillion profit to a ¥368 billion loss, and its shares have fallen about 25% since the seizure began.

events.headline: Colorado National Guard Rescues More Than 50 People From Historic Southwest Flooding
events.summary: Back-to-back historic floods on the San Juan, Animas, Dolores, Mancos and Navajo rivers pushed the Animas River's flow near Durango to roughly 50 times normal. The Colorado National Guard rescued more than 50 people and 20 pets by helicopter, and at least one death has been confirmed with a second suspected; cleanup continues.

events.headline: Florida National Guard Deployed as South Florida Flooding Tops 15 Inches of Rain, Shuts Schools
events.summary: Up to 15 inches of rain fell over Broward County between November 17-19, 2026, flooding homes and roads and prompting states of emergency in Broward County, Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood. Governor DeSantis mobilized hundreds of National Guard members with 50 high-water vehicles, airboats and swamp buggies; schools across Broward, Miami-Dade, Brevard, Volusia and Indian River counties closed, with flood watches continuing.

events.headline: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Judges Strip Chief Justice Święczkowski of Immunity
events.summary: The General Assembly of judges at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal voted on November 17, 2026 (announced November 18) to strip suspended tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski of immunity in four cases, opening the way for criminal charges over alleged unauthorized surveillance use. The move deepens a constitutional crisis between PM Tusk's government and the nationalist opposition and President Nawrocki.

events.headline: Russia Launches 141-Drone Barrage on Kyiv, Injuring Civilians
events.summary: Russia launched 141 drones at Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight Nov 17-18; Ukrainian air defense downed or suppressed 126. Debris hit a 28-story residential building in Kyiv's Pechersk district injuring three people, while an attack on Novi Petrivtsi in Kyiv Oblast injured four including a child and destroyed two houses.

events.headline: California Prosecutors From 30 Counties Petition Supreme Court to Halt Newsom Commutations
events.summary: Prosecutors representing 30 of California's 58 counties formally petitioned the state Supreme Court to halt Governor Newsom's commutation of 548 death sentences, arguing he exceeded his clemency authority and denied victims' families required hearing opportunities. Newsom's office maintains his authority does not trigger individual notice requirements.

events.headline: Trump Fires National Cyber Director Cairncross Amid Wave of Tech Outages
events.summary: The White House confirmed on November 19, 2026 that National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired with Trump's support, following a wave of tech outages including a global Microsoft outage, disruption to roughly 18,000 flights, and an NSA internal network crash that drew criticism of his cybersecurity oversight.

events.headline: Calls Mount for WV Auditor Mark Hunt to Resign; Morrisey Pursues Impeachment
events.summary: Following Mark Hunt's federal indictment on theft and fraud charges, State Treasurer Larry Pack publicly called for his resignation, and Governor Morrisey directed the DMV to refer additional violations tied to Hunt's used-car dealership to federal prosecutors while pursuing impeachment with the House of Delegates. The WV GOP and Democratic Party chairs, Secretary of State and Attorney General have also urged Hunt to resign; he has refused.

events.headline: Minnesota House DFL Picks Stephenson as Speaker-Designate Ahead of Expanded Majority
events.summary: Minnesota House Democrats selected Rep. Zack Stephenson as speaker-designate and Jamie Long as majority leader heading into a projected 77-57 DFL majority, the party's largest since 2009-10. House Republicans elected Rep. Harry Niska as minority leader.

events.headline: Washington Confirms $4 Billion Budget Shortfall, Orders Up to 15% Cuts
events.summary: Washington's November revenue forecast confirmed a $4 billion shortfall for the next fiscal year, worsened by federal health-care funding cuts. Governor Ferguson directed agency leaders to submit options for up to 15% additional spending cuts by November 23, with hiring, travel and contract freezes continuing and a full budget proposal due December 20.

events.headline: Inter-Jihadist Clashes Between ISSP and JNIM Escalate to Highest Level Since 2023 in Burkina Faso
events.summary: ISSP killed 46 JNIM militants on Nov 9 in the deadliest inter-jihadist clash since July 2023, part of a November escalation that has killed at least 63 militants in total. Reports indicate 500-700 ISSP reinforcements are moving in from Niger while JNIM convenes a council to send reinforcements from Mali.

events.headline: ASEAN Extends Myanmar Junta Travel Ban, Citing Failed 2021 Peace Plan
events.summary: Southeast Asian leaders extended a travel ban on Myanmar's junta leadership at the ASEAN summit, citing the failure of the 2021 peace plan. UN Secretary-General Guterres said engagement 'is not appeasement,' citing 3.7 million displaced and over 8,100 killed since the 2021 coup.

events.headline: EU Commission Proposes €45 Billion Ukraine Loan for 2027
events.summary: The European Commission adopted proposals for up to €45 billion in additional financing for Ukraine in 2027, split between €25 billion for military needs and €20 billion in reform-linked budget support, covering about two-thirds of Ukraine's estimated €70 billion financing gap. Ukraine would repay the principal only after Russia pays war reparations.

events.headline: New Zealand's Closest-Ever Election Remains Undeclared as Official Count Awaited
events.summary: New Zealand's Nov 7, 2026 general election remains undecided, with official results including about 400,000 special votes due Nov 27. On preliminary results, the incumbent National-ACT-NZ First coalition under PM Luxon holds 67 of 131 seats, just one seat over the majority threshold, making it one of the closest elections in the country's history.

events.headline: Russian Military Aircraft Enter Taiwan's Air Defense Zone, Trigger Regional Alerts
events.summary: Two sorties of Russian military aircraft entered Taiwan's air defense identification zone from the northeast and transited east of the island, triggering airspace alerts in Japan and South Korea as well.

events.headline: Oregon Attorney General Sues OpenAI for Over $2 Billion, Alleging ChatGPT Endangered Children
events.summary: Oregon AG Dan Rayfield filed suit Nov 17 in Multnomah County Circuit Court seeking about $2.035 billion from OpenAI, alleging the company fostered dependence in minors, used weak age verification, and misled parents about safety amid cases of children allegedly encouraged toward self-harm. The suit is separate from California's own OpenAI lawsuit, with a different plaintiff, court and claims.

events.headline: Sen. Louise Lucas Pleads Not Guilty, Seeks Sanctions Against Federal Officials
events.summary: Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas formally pleaded not guilty to federal racketeering, drug-distribution and money-laundering charges alleging she used her legislative position to protect a marijuana distribution operation. Her legal team has filed a motion seeking sanctions against Attorney General Todd Blanche, FBI Director Kash Patel and a top federal prosecutor over public statements; trial is set for mid-September 2027.

events.headline: Libya's Eastern Parliament Approves Turkey Maritime Deal as Egypt and Libya Sign Nine Pacts
events.summary: Libya's eastern House of Representatives reversed years of opposition and voted to adopt the 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum. Separately on November 19, Egypt's El-Sisi hosted Libyan PM Dbeibah in Cairo, signing nine bilateral cooperation agreements; Egypt maintains the Turkey-Libya deal is 'null, with no legal standing.'

events.headline: UK Inflation Hits 1-Year High of 3.6% as BAE Systems Cuts Up to 1,070 Jobs
events.summary: The UK's ONS reported on November 18, 2026 that CPI inflation rose to 3.6% year-on-year in October, from 3.5%, the fourth consecutive monthly increase, driven by transport and fuel costs. Separately, BAE Systems announced plans to cut up to 1,070 UK jobs across its air division, mainly in northwest England, and its head office.

events.headline: US Report Flags Taiwan's Nov 28 Local Elections as Test of China's Coercion Strategy
events.summary: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission's annual report to Congress says Beijing is watching Taiwan's November 28 local elections, and the 2028 presidential race, to gauge whether its coercion campaign is shifting opinion toward unification. It warns China could escalate to a blockade or quarantine if it judges the strategy to be failing; Taiwanese officials have separately warned of Chinese election interference via disinformation, AI and local proxies.

events.headline: New York Unveils Statewide Advanced Nuclear Master Plan Targeting 5 Gigawatts
events.summary: Gov. Hochul announced completion of a 30-point Advanced Nuclear Master Plan at a NYSERDA summit in Rochester on Nov 18, targeting 5 GW of new advanced nuclear capacity in addition to the state's existing 3.4 GW, and naming interested host communities.

events.headline: Developing Coastal Storm Threatens Flooding From Florida to the Carolinas, Could Become Subtropical Storm Kyle
events.summary: A coastal low pressure system off the Southeast coast could develop into Subtropical or Tropical Storm Kyle, forecast to bring 5-10 inches of rain, coastal and tidal flooding, and strong winds from northeast Florida through Georgia and the Carolinas, with effects possibly reaching Virginia and New England around Nov 21-22.

events.headline: Army to Detonate Nearly 10,000 Pounds of Deteriorated Lead Azide Near Middletown, Iowa, Prompting Evacuation Advisory
events.summary: The US Army plans to detonate about 68 drums (roughly 10,000 pounds) of degraded, shock-sensitive lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant around noon Friday, Nov 20. An airborne lead-particle plume could extend about 100 miles, prompting evacuation recommendations for nearby Middletown residents; EPA permitted the detonation due to increased instability after about 20 years in storage.

events.headline: Port of New Orleans, Tanker Crew File Dueling Suits Over Mississippi River Collision
events.summary: The Port of New Orleans sued tanker owner Nave Shipping and manager Thome Ship Management for more than $1 million after the asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt suffered a steering failure and struck the moored riverboat American Heritage on November 13, capsizing it and sending about 100 people into the river. Four tanker crew members filed a separate federal negligence suit; the NTSB is investigating.

events.headline: Serbia's New Parliament Convenes; Long-Ruling Socialist Party Loses All Seats
events.summary: Serbia's 15th National Assembly held its constitutive session on Nov 17, with opposition Student List holding 140 of 250 seats after a historic election win over the long-ruling SNS. The Socialist Party of Serbia won only 2.16% of the vote, losing parliamentary representation for the first time ever.

events.headline: Iraq Reaches Compromise With Kataib Hezbollah Over Oil-Smuggling Standoff
events.summary: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi had readied security forces against Kataib Hezbollah over alleged state oil-smuggling. After Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani mediated, a compromise reached on November 19, 2026 deploys a mixed force of Iraqi army, Federal Police, Energy Police and PMF to Jurf al-Sakhar instead, averting armed confrontation.

events.headline: Ecuadorean Fishermen Sue US Over Deadly Pacific Drone Strike on Fishing Vessel
events.summary: Sixteen Ecuadorean fishermen filed a federal lawsuit in Pittsburgh alleging US drones struck and sank their vessel near the Galápagos Islands on March 17, 2026. The suit says Operation Southern Spear has killed more than 235 people in 71 strikes since September 2025.

events.headline: Ohio Senate Passes 24-Hour Waiting Period and Telemedicine Abortion-Pill Ban, Sends Bills to DeWine
events.summary: The Ohio Senate passed HB 347, imposing a 24-hour waiting period, and HB 324, banning telemedicine prescribing of mifepristone, both along party lines. The bills now head to Gov. DeWine; Democrats say the measures defy the 2023 voter-approved abortion-rights constitutional amendment.

events.headline: Brazilian Police Probe Vance-Linked Rockbridge Network Over Election Interference Claims
events.summary: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered a federal police inquiry into whether the Rockbridge Network, a US conservative donor network co-founded by VP JD Vance, illegally intervened in Brazil's presidential runoff to benefit Flávio Bolsonaro. The probe centers on contacts between Brazilian entrepreneurs and Rockbridge intermediaries; both sides deny involvement.

events.headline: Recount Confirms Democrat Joe Madge Defeats Incoming SC House Majority Leader Micah Caskey
events.summary: A state-mandated recount in South Carolina House District 89 confirmed Democrat Joe Madge defeated Republican Micah Caskey, who had been slated to become House Majority Leader, by roughly 100 votes (7,263 to 7,156), flipping the seat.

events.headline: Missouri Democrats Post Largest Legislative Gains Since 1974, Break GOP Supermajorities in Both Chambers
events.summary: Missouri Democrats flipped 16 House seats, cutting the GOP majority from 111-52 to 94-68, and two Senate seats, from 24-10 to 22-12, in the November midterms. It is the largest House gain for Democrats since 1974 and ends a 14-year Republican legislative supermajority.

events.headline: John Deere to Close Ottumwa Works and Hagie Sprayer Plant in Clarion, Iowa, by 2029
events.summary: Deere & Company will end manufacturing at its century-old Ottumwa Works and the Hagie sprayer plant in Clarion, shifting production to Des Moines and Thibodaux, Louisiana, by fiscal year 2027-2029. The closures affect about 400 jobs in Ottumwa and 300 in Clarion; the UAW criticized the move ahead of 2027 contract talks.

events.headline: Three Twin Cities Churches Ask Federal Court to Release Records on ICE/DHS Surveillance of Congregants
events.summary: First Universalist Church of Minneapolis, Hennepin Avenue United Methodist Church, and St. John the Evangelist Episcopal Church sought release of DHS surveillance records tied to 'Operation Metro Surge,' after learning agents allegedly attended church meetings undercover and scanned attendees' license plates.

events.headline: 10th Circuit Hears Arguments Over Tulsa's Authority to Prosecute Non-Muscogee Native Americans
events.summary: The 10th Circuit Court of Appeals heard oral arguments Nov 18 in Muscogee Nation v. Kunzweiler over whether Oklahoma and Tulsa can prosecute non-Muscogee Native Americans within the Muscogee reservation, which covers most of Tulsa. The Cherokee, Chickasaw and Choctaw Nations filed briefs supporting the Muscogee Nation's position.

events.headline: Marana, Arizona Approves Final Business License for ICE Detention Facility Run by MTC
events.summary: The Town of Marana issued a business license Nov 18 to Management & Training Corporation to operate an immigration detention facility in a former state prison, clearing the last bureaucratic hurdle despite community opposition and controversy over an omitted sexual-abuse audit involving the operator.

events.headline: Texas Gov.-Elect Gina Hinojosa Vows to Return Local Control to State-Takeover School Districts
events.summary: In a Nov 18 interview, Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa said she will begin returning local control to the eight Texas districts and municipalities currently under state takeover after taking office Jan 19, singling out Houston ISD as a priority. The pledge follows Democrats sweeping every statewide office in Texas.

events.headline: PG&E Permanently Eliminates 208 Jobs Across California After Wildfire Liability Reform Fails in Legislature
events.summary: PG&E filed WARN notices eliminating 208 jobs across 65 California locations, including 125 in the Bay Area, following a strategic review after the legislature failed to pass wildfire liability reform. The utility is also deferring about $2 billion in planned 2027 capital spending.

events.headline: El Niño-Driven Flooding Intensifies Across East and Southern Africa
events.summary: A strengthening 'Super El Niño' combined with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole has driven heavy rainfall and flooding across Kenya's Tana River region, parts of Somalia and Tanzania, and South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal and Free State provinces. Forecasters warn of up to a 90% chance of above-normal rainfall continuing through December, with up to 874,000 people potentially displaced in Somalia alone between October and December 2026.

events.headline: Fresh Cholera Cases Reach Outskirts of Kinshasa Amid DRC's Worst Outbreak in Decades
events.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros confirmed the DRC has recorded over 60,000 cholera cases and about 1,800 deaths since the start of 2026, its worst outbreak in decades with roughly 3% mortality. Three fresh cases were detected in Kingabwa on Kinshasa's eastern outskirts, raising fears of spread into the densely populated capital during rainy season.

events.headline: EU Adds 30 Individuals and Two Entities to Russia Hybrid/Cyber Sanctions List
events.summary: On November 16, 2026, the EU Council added 30 individuals and two entities — including Russia's Social Design Agency and hacker group NoName057(16) — to its sanctions list targeting foreign information manipulation and malicious cyber activity linked to Russia. It is the largest such package to date, with a further broad sanctions package expected at the November 26-27 European Council summit.

events.headline: Pakistani Security Forces Kill 22 Militants in Raids Near Afghan Border
events.summary: Pakistan's military said intelligence-based raids between November 16-19, 2026 on militant hideouts in South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa killed 22 militants, which it alleged were India-backed. This follows a reported 74 militants killed in similar raids the previous week.

events.headline: 'Coalition of the Willing' Summit Convenes in Berlin on Ukraine Support
events.summary: Chancellor Merz hosted about 30 heads of state or government plus President Zelensky in Berlin on Nov 19 for a summit on Ukraine support and European security. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner briefed allies on the concurrent Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral talks, with 2027 defense funding and security guarantees on the agenda.

events.headline: ISIS-Linked ADF Gunmen Kill at Least 44 Civilians in DRC's Ituri Province
events.summary: ISIS-linked ADF militants killed at least 44 civilians across multiple villages in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, in attacks confirmed through November 17. The toll climbed from an initial count of about 22 during the week.
events.locationName: Mambasa, Ituri, Democratic Republic of Congo

events.headline: All 36 Nigerian State Assemblies Approve Constitutional Amendment Creating State Police
events.summary: All 36 Nigerian state assemblies have approved a constitutional amendment establishing state police forces, sending the bill to President Tinubu for assent.

events.headline: Baltic States and Finland Issue Drone Shelter Alerts Amid Russia-Ukraine Strikes
events.summary: Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia briefly issued shelter alerts and NATO scrambled fighter jets after drones entered Baltic airspace from Russia and Belarus amid a Ukrainian strike on the Ust-Luga port. Finland imposed, then lifted, temporary airspace and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland; no injuries were reported.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Hits 4% in October, Cementing December ECB Hike Expectations
events.summary: Euro-area inflation rose to 4% in October 2026, up from 3.8%, marking a three-year high driven by energy prices surging over 20%. Markets now price a greater than 90% probability of a further ECB rate hike in December.

events.headline: Hegseth Delivers First C-130 to Colombian Military Amid Friction Over Joint US Operations
events.summary: Hegseth traveled to Bogotá on Nov 18, handing over the first of several promised C-130 Hercules aircraft to the Colombian Air Force and meeting Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora. Reports emerged of friction within the Colombian government over the scope of joint US-Colombia counter-narcotics operations.

events.headline: Colombia Withdraws From Santa Marta Fossil-Fuel Phaseout Coalition
events.summary: Colombia's new right-wing government withdrew from the Santa Marta coalition, a 57-government fossil-fuel phaseout pact launched by predecessor Petro, as the coalition presses ahead without it amid COP31 talks in Antalya. The move follows President de la Espriella's pledge to revive oil and gas exploration.

events.headline: Reuters Traces 8,000-Plus Hoax Bomb Threats to Coordinated Pan-European Campaign
events.summary: A Reuters investigation found that over 8,000 hoax 'Death is near' bomb threats hit European schools, airports, airlines, and newsrooms over the past month, including roughly 6,300 Italian schools evacuated on Nov 11 and about 1,000 Scottish schools. The threats were falsely signed as Russian group 'Male State'; a suspect was arrested in Ukraine.

events.headline: RSF Commander Defects to Sudanese Army as Army Strikes RSF Headquarters in Nyala
events.summary: Mishal Abdelrahman, an RSF commander of the 27th/28th groups, announced his defection to the Sudanese army on November 19, 2026, bringing troops with him, part of a wider pattern of RSF defections. The same day, Sudanese army drones and aircraft struck RSF headquarters in Nyala, South Darfur, while the army and RSF traded competing claims over control of Derang in Blue Nile State.

events.headline: Storm Charles Floods Spread From Madeira Across Southern Europe
events.summary: Storm Charles battered Madeira on Nov 10 with over 200mm of rain and 130km/h gusts, closing all Portuguese schools. The rain band then moved across southern France, causing flooding and rockfalls on the French Riviera, before hitting Switzerland, northern Italy, and Croatia through roughly Nov 14.

events.headline: Lula Signs Decree Ending Brazil's Six-Day Work Week
events.summary: President Lula signed a decree on November 19, 2026 implementing Constitutional Amendment 141, ending Brazil's 6x1 work schedule in favor of a 5x2 schedule. The transition begins December 16, 2026, cutting the maximum work week from 44 to 42 hours, with full transition to a 40-hour week planned for 2027.

events.headline: Canada's House of Commons Passes 2026 Federal Budget
events.summary: The House of Commons passed the Liberal government's 2026 federal budget on November 19, 2026 by a vote of 162-151. The budget includes new borrowing and spending for infrastructure; the NDP voted against it.

events.headline: Panama Declares National Malaria Health Alert After Capital-Area Outbreak
events.summary: Panama's Ministry of Health declared a national malaria health alert on November 16, 2026 after 161 cases were confirmed in the Ancón district of Panama City, an area not normally endemic for the disease. A priority epidemiological cordon was established in the Metropolitan Health Region; regional case counts remain far higher in Panamá Este (3,053), Guna Yala (2,016) and Darién (1,162).

events.headline: Nordic Nations Agree to Draft Formal Nordic Defence Cooperation Agreement
events.summary: Defence ministers of Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and Iceland, meeting in Oslo on November 11-12, 2026, agreed to begin drafting a formal Nordic Defence Cooperation Agreement for deeper joint military operations and procurement. The nations are on track to triple joint ammunition production capacity by 2030, including a roughly $155 million Nammo AS partnership.

events.headline: Senegal's Ruling Party Pastef Formally Expels President Faye and 31 Others
events.summary: Pastef-Les Patriotes' National Council confirmed on November 17-18, 2026 the automatic expulsion of President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and 31 other 'inactive members,' deepening the rift between Faye and party leader Ousmane Sonko. Sonko's Pastef holds 130 of 165 National Assembly seats while Faye's new party has none, creating a parliamentary deadlock that threatens IMF aid and the 2027 budget.

events.headline: Thailand Flood Death Toll Reaches 89 as New Heavy-Rain Warning Issued for South
events.summary: Thailand's disaster agency reported 89 flood-related deaths and about 48,700 households, roughly 121,400 people, affected as of November 15, 2026, across Chumphon, Lop Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Ayutthaya and Suphan Buri. The Thai Meteorological Department issued a fresh warning on November 19 for heavy rain across southern provinces through November 22.

events.headline: Colombia Holds Nationwide Strike Against 'Economic Rescue Law' Fiscal Bill
events.summary: Colombia's largest union federation CUT and teachers' union FECODE, backed by Pacto Histórico, called a 24-hour national strike for Nov 19 against President de la Espriella's fiscal bill raising VAT and income tax while cutting spending. The US Embassy issued a security advisory, while the IMF has endorsed the bill.

events.headline: Peru Declares Nationwide 8-Month Fuel-Supply Emergency Over El Niño Risk
events.summary: Peru's Energy and Mines Ministry declared an emergency across the national hydrocarbon supply chain for up to eight months, citing risk of flooding and landslides from the 2026-2027 El Niño damaging critical infrastructure. Roughly 67% of Peru's energy matrix depends on this supply chain.

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Tatarstan Oil Hub and Krasnodar Refineries
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan, which handles roughly 30% of Russia's crude flow toward the Druzhba pipeline, overnight Nov 18-19. Earlier strikes also hit the Ilsky and Afipsky refineries in Krasnodar Krai, part of a sustained campaign that has disrupted 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries over 20 days.

events.headline: Sudanese Army Advances Within 60km of RSF Stronghold Al Nuhud After Capturing Al-Khuwai
events.summary: Sudan's army and allied forces captured Al-Khuwai, the first West Kordofan city to fall to the army in its current offensive, advancing to within roughly 60km of the major RSF stronghold Al Nuhud. The army has retaken over 30 villages and towns since early November, while a Joint Force repelled an RSF attack in North Darfur.

events.headline: Myanmar Military Airstrikes Kill 14 Civilians Over Four Days in Rakhine and Chin States
events.summary: Myanmar's military conducted airstrikes over four consecutive days, Nov 14-17, across Rakhine State and Paletwa Township in Chin State, killing 14 civilians and injuring 28, according to the Arakan Army. The deadliest strike occurred Nov 14 in Paletwa, where four fighter jets and a Y-12 aircraft bombed for over an hour, killing 12 and injuring 21, including a pregnant woman and a child.

events.headline: Fresh Flooding Kills Up to 12 in Khanh Hoa Province, Central Vietnam
events.summary: A new wave of heavy rain and flooding hit Khanh Hoa province and Nha Trang city overnight into Nov 19, leaving 9 to 12 people dead or missing depending on the source, with 16,000 to over 20,000 households evacuated or affected. Estimated damage in Khanh Hoa alone reached roughly VND 372 billion (about $14.1 million).
events.locationName: Nha Trang, Khanh Hoa Province, Vietnam

events.headline: El Niño Floods and Landslides Affect Over 77,000 People Across Ecuador
events.summary: Flooding and landslides linked to El Niño have affected 77,510 people across Ecuador since August 29, killing 14 and damaging more than 21,200 homes. Guayas, El Oro, Galápagos and Manabí provinces are among the hardest hit.

events.headline: Watchdog: Hochul's NYC Transit Fund Cut Shifts $200M Burden to MTA
events.summary: A watchdog report found New York state's $200 million one-time reduction in New York City's annual payment to the MTA bus division is being absorbed by the MTA rather than backfilled, worsening its structural deficit, projected near $897 million by 2030. The state's three-year budget gap narrowed to $8.9 billion from $14.7 billion, aiding efforts to close NYC's roughly $6.2 billion deficit.

events.headline: Chicago Judge Vacates 1992 Murder Conviction, Citing Police Torture
events.summary: Cook County Judge Adrienne Davis vacated Anthony Garrett's conviction in the 1992 killing of 7-year-old Dantrell Davis, finding former detective Richard Zuley tortured Garrett into a coerced confession. The judge ordered a retrial.

events.headline: Brazil Police Crisis Deepens Over Supreme Court-Banco Master Probe Reports
events.summary: Brazil's Federal Police director-general removed two anti-corruption unit chiefs after they produced reports mentioning Supreme Court justices found in phone and financial records tied to jailed former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro. Police denied political interference; revised reports were handed to Supreme Court president Edson Fachin on November 18, and the Senate held hearings the same day.

events.headline: West Virginia Regulators Approve $2.48 Billion Natural Gas Plant at Fort Martin
events.summary: The West Virginia Public Service Commission approved Mon Power and Potomac Edison's $2.48 billion, 1,200-megawatt combined-cycle gas plant plus $182 million in new solar projects across three counties. Customers will see a monthly surcharge starting at $1.18.

events.headline: Ohio Gov. DeWine Reviewing Clemency for More Than a Dozen Death-Row Inmates
events.summary: Governor Mike DeWine initiated clemency reviews for death sentences from at least 10 counties before leaving office in January 2027, though no commutations have been finalized. Prosecutors have objected to the timeline, while the ACLU of Ohio has welcomed the reviews.

events.headline: PNG's Marape Tells Xi Closing Taiwan Office 'Wasn't Easy'; Floats Three-Child Policy
events.summary: On the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 17, 2026, PNG PM James Marape told Xi Jinping that closing Taiwan's de facto representative office in PNG 'wasn't easy,' after Taiwan said it shut the office and halted PNG LNG purchases citing Chinese pressure. Marape separately floated a National Family Planning Policy encouraging families to limit to three children to curb PNG's 2.6% annual population growth, later clarifying it as a discussion proposal rather than formal policy.

events.headline: Israel Strikes Underground Hezbollah Missile Site Near Janta, Eastern Lebanon
events.summary: On the evening of November 19, 2026, the Israeli Air Force struck entrances to an underground Hezbollah missile production and storage facility in the Al-Shaara area near Janta village. The IDF said it struck after detecting Hezbollah operatives returning to rehabilitate the site; it follows an earlier November 8 strike on a weapons shipment in the same general area. No casualties were reported.

events.headline: Salt Lake City Enacts 6-Month Data Center Moratorium as Utah Lawmakers Draft Statewide Rules
events.summary: The Salt Lake City Council unanimously passed a 180-day moratorium on new data-center permits Nov 17, citing air, noise and light pollution and utility-strain concerns. Separately, state lawmakers released a draft proposal for the 2027 legislative session to add statewide water, energy and local-control rules for data centers, which is not yet enacted.

events.headline: New Migrant Caravan Departs Honduras for US Border
events.summary: A new caravan, the fourth since September, of roughly 100 to 400 migrants left San Pedro Sula, Honduras on Nov 15-16, entering Guatemala and then Mexico. The group includes migrants from Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Cuba, and Haiti.

events.headline: Arkansas Gov. Sanders Announces $261 Million for 75 Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Projects
events.summary: Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders announced $261,103,410 in state financial assistance for 75 water and wastewater infrastructure projects statewide, projected to benefit more than 740,000 residents.

events.headline: Washington Court of Appeals Revives Seattle Landlord's Takings Challenge to City Rent Regulations
events.summary: The Washington Court of Appeals, Division One, ruled Oct 26 that GRE Downtowner LLC, owner of the 254-unit Addison on Fourth affordable-housing project in Seattle's Chinatown-International District, can proceed with claims that the combined effect of Seattle's eviction, rent-notice and relocation-assistance ordinances amounted to an unconstitutional regulatory taking. The ruling reverses a lower-court dismissal but does not determine compensation owed.

events.headline: Cape Verde's Neves Wins Re-Election Outright With 63.8% in First Round
events.summary: President José Maria Neves won re-election outright in the first round with 63.8% of the provisional vote (97% counted), defeating five challengers including first-time woman candidate Joana Rosa Amado, who took 31.5%.

events.headline: Measles Virus Detected in Stamford-Darien Wastewater, Connecticut Health Officials Say
events.summary: Connecticut's Department of Public Health announced Nov 18-19 that measles virus was detected in a sewershed serving Stamford and Darien, an early-warning surveillance signal rather than confirmation of an active outbreak. The state has recorded three confirmed measles cases in 2026.

events.headline: Teamsters Strike at Associated Grocers Northeast Enters Third Week, Empty Shelves Across New England
events.summary: The Teamsters Local 633 strike at the Associated Grocers Northeast distribution center in Pembroke, which began Nov 5 over a pension-versus-401k dispute, is in its third week as of Nov 17-19. Federal mediation is resuming while empty shelves persist at roughly 1,000 member stores across New England and New York.

events.headline: Virginia's First Statewide Climate Assessment Warns of Rising Seas, Economic Risk to Tidewater
events.summary: George Mason University's Virginia Climate Center report warns of accelerating warming and among the fastest sea-level rise rates on the East Coast, with billions in wages and hundreds of thousands of Tidewater jobs exposed to tidal flooding by 2050. The assessment, Virginia's first statewide one, has circulated again in local coverage this month.

events.headline: NC Labor Department Sues Durham Nonprofit Founder Courtney Jordan Over $91,000 in Unpaid Wages
events.summary: North Carolina's Labor Commissioner's office sued CJF America and executives Courtney Jordan, Nick Gallardo, Kristen Picot and Rhoda Hormenoo, seeking more than $91,000 in unpaid wages owed to 13 former summer-camp workers.

events.headline: Seminole County Officials Clarify Vote-Tabulation Delay That Briefly Appeared to Flip Georgia House District 154
events.summary: Officials said a data-upload delay, not a missing memory card, temporarily affected reporting of about 388 Election Day votes in Seminole County's House District 154 race, briefly putting GOP incumbent Gerald Greene ahead of Democrat Harry James. A hand-count audit confirmed the originally certified Nov 6 results, with no change to the outcome.

events.headline: Hundreds Rally at Illinois Capitol for POWER Act to Regulate Data Center Energy and Water Use
events.summary: About 600 advocates, faith leaders and lawmakers rallied at the Illinois Capitol on Nov 18 for the POWER Act, which would require data centers to fund their own grid connections and power, disclose water use, and limit generator noise. A Senate committee held a hearing the same day but has not voted; the veto session ends Dec 3.

events.headline: IMF Reaches $2.3 Billion Staff-Level Disbursement Agreement With Egypt
events.summary: The IMF and Egypt reached a staff-level agreement on November 18-19, 2026 unlocking roughly $2.3 billion, about $1.5 billion under the Extended Fund Facility and $0.8 billion under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, as Egypt's $8 billion loan program nears its December 15 expiry. The IMF cited resilient 5.1% GDP growth.

events.headline: Storm Downs Transmission Towers, Cutting Power to Tens of Thousands on Australia's Eyre Peninsula
events.summary: A severe storm struck South Australia's Eyre Peninsula around 3pm on November 19, 2026, downing multiple 132kV and 270kV transmission towers between Cultana and Port Lincoln and cutting power to a peak of about 24,000-30,000 properties. Premier Malinauskas said the main transmission line could take 'days' to restore; an emergency cabinet was declared to activate backup generators, and an independent examination into operator ElectraNet was announced.

events.headline: UN Releases $18 Million From Emergency Fund for Afghanistan Winter Aid
events.summary: The UN Emergency Relief Coordinator approved the release of $18 million from the Central Emergency Response Fund to support 824,000 people in Afghanistan through the 2026-27 winter. The funding covers seven projects in food security, health, nutrition, protection, shelter, and WASH, part of a broader $48 million response amid severe shortfalls in Afghanistan's humanitarian plan covering 21.9 million people in need.

events.headline: Kauai Closes Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program to New Applicants Amid High Demand
events.summary: As of Nov 18-19, Kauai County's Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program stopped accepting new applications due to high demand, though a waitlist remains open. The state's Emergency Farmer Relief program continues accepting applications of up to $1,500 through Jan 29, 2027, and property owners have until June 30, 2027 to file for disaster tax relief.

events.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo Hold First Head-to-Head TV Debate Ahead of Spain's Nov 29 Election
events.summary: Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez and opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo held their first one-on-one televised debate on November 19, 2026, ahead of the November 29 general election.

events.headline: Armenia Launches Biometric Passports as Pashinyan Signals CSTO Exit Drift
events.summary: Armenia began issuing EU-standard biometric passports and ID cards on Nov 1 as part of its EU visa-liberalization process. PM Pashinyan said Armenia's interest in the CSTO 'has run its course,' prompting the bloc to strip Armenia of voting rights and senior positions on Nov 11, though no formal withdrawal notice has been filed.

events.headline: Missing Ugandan Opposition Activist Sam Mugumya Surfaces, Charged With Treachery Over Alleged ADF Links
events.summary: Ugandan opposition activist Sam Mugumya appeared before a military court on Nov 18, about 15 months after his alleged abduction, charged alongside two UPDF soldiers with treachery for allegedly soliciting soldiers to coordinate with ADF rebels. All three denied the charges and were remanded until Dec 21; treachery carries a potential death sentence.

events.headline: Two Syrian Security Personnel Killed in Shootout During Jaramana Arrest Raid
events.summary: Two Syrian security personnel were killed and four wounded during an attempted arrest in Jaramana, Damascus countryside, when a wanted suspect accused of shooting his father and an accomplice opened fire. Both attackers were killed in the return fire.

events.headline: South Africa's JSE Suffers Sharp One-Day Drop Led by Gold and Platinum Miners
events.summary: South Africa's JSE retreated about 3% over Nov 18-19, led by declines in precious-metals miners including AngloGold Ashanti (down 4.5%) and Harmony Gold (down 3.6%), as gold prices pulled back. The rand weakened to roughly R17.15-17.18 per dollar amid broader dollar strength.

events.headline: US-Somali Forces Kill Al-Shabaab Finance Chief, Wound Three Commanders in Airstrikes
events.summary: AFRICOM, coordinating with Somalia's federal government, conducted airstrikes near Yaaq Shiniile on November 17, 2026. Separate strikes in Somalia's Hiraan region killed two al-Shabaab members, including finance chief 'Ismaaciil,' and seriously wounded three other commanders.

events.headline: Indonesia: Yogyakarta Protest Crackdown as VP Seat Stays Vacant Ahead of Dec 9 Vote
events.summary: Protests in Yogyakarta against President Prabowo over corruption, cost of living and forest-fire management turned violent on November 10, 2026, with police using rubber bullets, water cannon and tear gas; 157 people were detained. Indonesia's vice-presidential seat has been vacant since Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation on November 12, with the MPR rescheduling its plenary session to elect a successor to December 9, 2026.

events.headline: Lima Bus Driver Killed by Extortionists, Sparking Transit Workers' Strike
events.summary: Driver José Miranda of the Los Mandarinos transport company was shot dead in Jicamarca, Lima, by gunmen posing as passengers in an apparent extortion attack. Over 200 coworkers suspended service and marched to the Interior Ministry, while more than 50 Lima transport companies halted operations amid rising extortion violence.

events.headline: Winter Storm Knocks Out Power to Tens of Thousands, Downs Trees Across Northern California
events.summary: A powerful atmospheric-river storm swept Northern California on Nov 18, cutting power to tens of thousands of customers including over 32,000 SMUD customers in Sacramento and 18,000 PG&E customers in the Bay Area. The storm downed trees, flooded roads, and brought heavy Sierra snow, with one person injured by a falling limb in Angels Camp.

events.headline: Chile's CUT Union Leads National March Against Kast Government's 2027 Budget Cuts
events.summary: On Nov 18, Chile's CUT union federation and student confederation Confech led a national day of protest in Santiago and at 24 points nationwide against President Kast's 2027 budget cuts. Organizers announced a follow-up protest calendar including a teachers' strike on Nov 24 and housing and pension mobilizations later in the month.

events.headline: Libya's Parliament-Government Standoff Escalates After Zintan Airport Closure Blocks Session
events.summary: Libya's House of Representatives accused Tripoli's GNU Prime Minister Dabaiba of blocking flight permits that prevented lawmakers from reaching a scheduled Nov 16 session in Zintan after an airport closure. The HoR Speaker convened an emergency session in Benghazi on Nov 18, which the GNU rejected as illegitimate.

events.headline: Submarine Cable Fault Causes Nationwide Internet Disruption Across Pakistan
events.summary: A fault in the SEA-ME-WE 5 submarine cable about 11km off Pakistan's coast caused nationwide internet slowdowns starting Nov 18, with Cloudflare Radar data showing HTTP traffic down up to 36%. Pakistan's telecom regulator confirmed the fault and said the operator is rerouting traffic, with no restoration timeline given.

events.headline: World Bank: Afghanistan's Per-Capita Income Falls for Third Straight Year Despite GDP Growth
events.summary: The World Bank's November 2026 Afghanistan Development Update projects 3% GDP growth for fiscal year 2026, driven by agriculture, but per-capita income is declining 3.3% for a third consecutive year as population growth of 6.6% outpaces output. The report also flags severe water scarcity, with Afghanistan losing about 4.9 billion cubic meters of freshwater per year since 2003.

events.headline: Kim Jong Un Tours North Korean Naval University, Criticizes 'Enemy' Naval Activity
events.summary: Kim Jong Un visited the Kim Jong Suk Naval University and nearby development sites in South Hamgyong Province on Nov 17-18, with state media KCNA reporting he criticized naval activity by 'wicked enemies.' The visit came as Trump publicly renewed calls for a possible meeting with Kim during his China trip, though North Korean state media gave no direct response to the overture.

events.headline: Zambia's Cholera Outbreak Grows to Over 3,000 Cases, 68 Deaths
events.summary: Zambia's cholera outbreak, declared on July 28, 2026, has grown to 3,099 cumulative cases (437 confirmed) across 27 districts in seven provinces, with 68 deaths as of Nov 16 per national public health institute data. Lusaka is the worst-hit area with 1,959 cases.

events.headline: Australia's Unemployment Jumps to 4.9%, Fueling Recession Fears
events.summary: Australia's unemployment rate surged to 4.9% in October 2026 from 4.7%, a five-year high, prompting economists to warn the economy may be 'one foot in a recession' following the RBA's fifth rate hike this year. Collapsed retailer David Jones, in receivership since Nov 5 with $459 million in debt, confirmed it will close 19 of its 38 stores nationally, cutting 141 jobs including in Queensland.
